Owed to this implementing card by the spec seat, from the contract review of PR #34001 (card #33808; records https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/34001#issuecomment-6897177404 and https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/34001#issuecomment-6898419500). When #34001 merges, `IAIService`'s "in-app assistant door" section binds the in-app pending-action queue. Each item is decided only by the person it was queued for (`actorId` must equal `proposed_by`), for every queued item regardless of which trigger queued it. An administrator who must also approve does so through `held`.

What the implementation here must also do, because the contract text alone does not make it happen:
1. **Refuse to queue an in-app item without the person the call ran as.** `ProposePendingActionInput.proposedBy` stays optional in the contract (review flag 1, option A). An item queued with no recorded person would be decidable by nobody, which fails closed but leaves dead items. The route or service must refuse that queue write.
2. **Make the refusal of another user's decision a throw.** `approvePendingAction`'s `failed` already means an approved item whose execution failed. So a decision by someone other than `proposed_by`, on approve and on reject alike, has to throw, not return `failed`. Say so in the implementation's docblocks (review N1).
3. **Decide how an unanswered item lapses.** An in-app item whose person never answers, or has left, stays `pending`, because only that person may reject it. The hand-off text leaves lapse to the host; the in-app implementation should state its own lapse rule (review N2).

The changeset of #34001 marks this as BREAKING when the implementing change ships (ADR-0087 entry `in-app-pending-action-decided-by-person`). The release that carries this card's routes must say in its changelog that the door enforces it.
